name: Gas hydrate production
principle: Methane locked in ice-like hydrates is released by depressurisation, heating or CO2 exchange. Japan's JOGMEC produced gas offshore at Nankai Trough in March 2013 by depressurisation; Mallik (Canada) showed constant flow by lowering pressure in 2008; 1 m3 of hydrate releases about 164 m3 of methane.

process_steps.name: Produce gas and water; control sand

performance.metric: methane released per m3 of hydrate

performance.metric: Shenhu Area trial gas production, South China Sea (2017 and 2020 offshore production tests)
performance.unit: m3/day average (2017 trial; 2020 trial average over 30 days)
performance.basis: 2017 trial: over 300,000 m3 gas in 60 days, average daily extraction above 5,000 m3 (SCIO, 9 Jul 2017). 2020 trial: 861,400 m3 (86.14x10^4 m3) over 30 days of continuous production from 1,225 m water depth (US DOE/NETL International Gas Hydrate R&D Activities Update, Dec 2020); 861400/30 = 28,713 m3/day average

source.note: US DOE, International Gas Hydrate R&D Activities Update, 2 Dec 2020, China section (read 2026-10-28); 2017 trial from english.scio.gov.cn, 9 Jul 2017

costs.metric: unit cost of methane exploitation with the proposed reservoir-reconstruction method (simulation study)
costs.basis: dollar year not stated (publication 2025). Process-simulation study by China University of Petroleum (East China) and National University of Singapore (Baojiang Sun, Praveen Linga): the proposed method raises gas production about 73% vs conventional depressurization and could cut exploitation cost to as low as 0.46 USD/m3, dropping to about 0.14 USD/m3 under optimal porosity/saturation conditions; simulation result, capital cost not stated

source.note: EurekAlert! (Higher Education Press), New method proposed for offshore gas hydrate production, 23 Oct 2025 (read 2026-10-28)
